item.title: If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it
item.author: hi@cekrem.dev (Christian Ekrem)
item.description: Whatever skill you’re learning, it won’t take long before someone with experience in that particular field tells you to get your hands dirty. It’s fine to read “Born to Run”, but you won’t be running an ultra marathon any time soon if you don’t start running. Whether it’s muscle memory, technique, physical fitness or problem solving you need to work on to reach your goals, you need to practice. This isn’t a controversial statement in any field at all, and has never really been.

item.title: I'm as of now completely off the AI bandwagon (if I was ever remotely on it)
item.author: hi@cekrem.dev (Christian Ekrem)
item.description: Long time readers will know that I was never quite the AI fanboy in the first place (to put it mildly). I’ve written at length (and width) about software engineering and coding being a craft, not a problem now solved by the latest Anthropic model. But I’ve - of course! - experimented, and given LLMs a fair shot at being “the right tool for the job” in certain well-contained areas. While I don’t regret my exploration, I’ve come to realize I need to up my game a bit to stay sane, happy and smart. I need a clean cut that involves all LLM usage.

item.title: I Signed the 'No AI in Node.js Core' Petition
item.author: hi@cekrem.dev (Christian Ekrem)
item.description:
It’s Friday, and I just signed a petition asking the Node.js TSC to vote no on allowing AI-generated code in Node.js core.

Someone opened a 19,000-line pull request to rewrite Node.js internals, with the disclaimer that “a significant amount of Claude Code tokens” were used to create it. The author reviewed the changes themselves. (That’s the claim, anyway. And speaking of (dis)claim(ers): I don’t know the author of this PR or the quality of prior contributions, that’s beside the point! Probably a brilliant software engineer!)
